_comment: Measured, not estimated. Produced by tokenizing the exact bytes internal/bench.PromptText emits, wrapped in the served model's chat template. Recapture whenever promptCorpusSHA or the served model changes; both are inputs to every number here. WHAT IS NOT RECORDED: the tokenizer revision. An earlier version of this line said the tokenizer was 'at the recorded revision' and no revision is recorded anywhere -- not here, not in config/vllm-shared/engine-a.yaml, which names the model without a revision argument, and not in RunManifest.TokenizerRev, which is declared and never written. So these numbers identify a model name and a corpus hash, and cannot be tied to the exact tokenizer artifacts that produced them.

samples.role: standard, sized to land exactly on the guard's threshold

estimatorVerdict._why: The three measured ratios are 1.36, 0.774 and 0.770 -- monotone DECREASING, not non-monotone; an earlier version of this line said otherwise and its own samples do not support that. What they do establish is that no single multiplicative factor fits all three, because the ratios differ. The chat template costs a fixed overhead of roughly 25 tokens, which dominates a 200-character prompt: 50 estimated against 68 measured. The corpus itself runs about 5.2 characters per token, so at 40,000 characters the same formula gives 10,000 estimated against 7,695 measured. QUOTE THE PAIRS, NOT A PERCENTAGE: the two errors are conventionally normalised against different denominators (36 percent of the estimate at 200 characters, 30 percent of the measurement at 40,000), and that mismatch put a wrong figure into seven comments in this repository. The design spec's claim that len/4 is conservative holds only in the long regime.
estimatorVerdict._falsePositiveBand: A request the guard scores at exactly 4096 was measured at 3171 real tokens, so requests whose true input is between 3171 and 4096 tokens are rejected as though they had crossed. The band is 925 tokens, 22.6 percent of the threshold, and it costs a tenant service rather than costing the cache. Reported rather than corrected: the threshold was pre-registered, and moving it after measuring is exactly the post-hoc tuning the control arm exists to rule out.

tokenizerSharedWithVerified: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct at revision a09a35458c702b33eeacc393d103063234e8bc28 carries BYTE-IDENTICAL merges.txt, tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json and vocab.json: all four per-file sha256 values match the ones above exactly. That is the claim, and it does not depend on how the four are combined -- both combining conventions tried gave one value for both models, because the inputs were equal. The two REPOSITORY revisions differ (aa8e7253... against a09a3545...), so the repo sha alone would have said nothing here. Measured 2026-09-30, tokenizer files only, no weights.
_identityNote: Two identities, and they fix different things. tokenizerRevision is the upstream repository revision: it changes when the weights change even if the tokenizer does not, and it changes if the tokenizer moves. tokenizerCoreFilesCombinedSHA256 fixes the tokenizer bytes themselves and is the stronger claim. RunManifest.TokenizerRev carries the revision, because a manifest names where something came from and a reader can fetch that revision and recompute these hashes. Measured 2026-09-30, over the files at that revision, weights not downloaded.
tokenizerCoreFilesCombinedSHA256Definiti: sha256 over the concatenation, for merges.txt, tokenizer.json, tokenizer_config.json and vocab.json in that byte order of their names, of the string "<lowercase hex sha256 of the file>  <file name>\n" -- two spaces, as sha256sum prints. WRITTEN DOWN BECAUSE IT WAS NOT. A shell pipeline computing the same idea with a different sort key produced 109e0f26695b0b14... for these exact files, and this field held that value briefly while the recorded one was 81feaac8d04514a2... Two values for one name is how a number stops being checkable, and the fix is the definition, not the digest.
